findings.text: The kernel_cap_t privilege set is a tiny value type wrapping a single 64 [CITED] bit word, so whole sets copy by value. The cpu_vfs_cap_data filesystem record combines a magic and flag word with the owning root identity plus separate permitted and inheritable sets of that type.

The kernel to user capability handshake selects version 3 [CITED] of the defined interface. The user header length and the kernel set length are each defined as the storage size of their corresponding structure, keeping wire and in memory footprints tied to the type definitions rather than to fixed literals.

A filesystem oriented privilege grouping gathers ownership, node creation, discretionary access override and search, file ownership, set identity handling and mandatory access override. Empty denotes no privileges and full denotes every valid privilege; two derived groupings extend the filesystem grouping, one toward immutable file handling and one toward server resource control. Helpers provide clearing a set, setting or clearing an individual member, testing membership, union, intersection, difference, emptiness, equality and subset relation, plus dropping a whole derived grouping or restoring only those members of it that also appear in a permitted mask.

The fragments export inline privilege queries keyed by task, user namespace and privilege number, in auditing and silent forms, plus current context and set identity variants, together with composite checks for performance monitoring, packet filtering and checkpoint restore that each accept either a dedicated privilege or system administration.

In the routed configuration every base privilege query unconditionally reports success, so namespace, audit and set identity distinctions have no effect here. The composite monitoring, filtering and restore helpers therefore reduce to a disjunction of always successful checks.

Callers invoke the base queries with a task, an optional namespace and a privilege number and receive a boolean allow decision, choosing auditing or silent forms and current context or set identity variants; composite callers invoke the parameterless monitoring and filtering checks or the namespace scoped restore checks and receive the disjunctive result.

Control group type names are limited to 32 [CITED] characters, while hierarchy names and control file type names are each limited to 64 [CITED] characters, bounding the corresponding fixed size arrays.

Subsystem identifiers of cgroup_subsys_id are generated by stamping a suffix onto each name listed in a separate subsystem catalogue, collected into an enumeration terminated by a count sentinel that also sizes per subsystem arrays elsewhere.

A subsystem state carries lifecycle marks for opting out of reference counting, being between online and offline transitions, having released its last reference, being visible to user space, and being in teardown. Online and released plus dying describe progression toward reclamation, while visibility gates user space exposure.

Per group behavioral marks request release notification to user space, cloning of parent configuration for processor set children, a desired frozen condition, and the observed frozen condition. Desired versus observed allows a request to persist while descendants drain toward the frozen state.

Hierarchy wide options control whether mounted subsystems omit name prefixes, whether extended attributes are supported, whether namespaces act as delegation boundaries for controller files, whether dynamic modification latency is favored over fork and exit cost, whether the processor set controller uses newer semantics, and whether legacy local event, recursive protection and accounting behaviors are enabled for memory and process number controllers.

Control file visibility and writability are governed by marks for root only, non root only, delegation crossing, omitted subsystem prefix, world writable legacy, debug only, and internal default hierarchy only or excluded plus an added marker. Attachment locking offers a global mode, a no lock mode for self attachment without thread group scope, and a per thread group mode used when dynamic modification favoring is active.

The cgroup_file handle pairs its filesystem node with a notification timestamp, a timer and a spin lock. The css_rstat_cpu per processor linkage chains updated children through a parent pointer and sibling link plus a lockless queue node and back pointer. The cgroup_base_stat accounting accumulates processor time and a monotonic event count with optional idle accumulation, while cgroup_rstat_base_cpu adds synchronized current values plus snapshots of last and subtree totals for delta propagation.

The cgroup_subsys_state combines identity in the form of a subsystem unique number with root reserved, flag bits and a global serial that orders every state and its child lists, with hierarchy anchors to its group, subsystem, parent and sibling and child links. Lifetime management uses reference counting, an online counter that pins parents while children stay online, process and RCU deferred destruction work, and a visible descendant count. Accounting and population state adds per processor statistic areas, populated set and child counters, a deferred finish work item, and a scratch link reserved for statistic flushing.

The css_set task sharing group holds an immutable per subsystem state vector sized by the subsystem count, a reference count, hash linkage and RCU reclamation. Placement state records a domain sharing group with self for domain groups and nearest domain ancestor for threaded groups, a default group, links to referenced groups, reverse membership per subsystem, and threaded peer lists. Task state counts internal tasks and maintains active, migrating and dying lists plus active iterators. Migration state adds source and destination preload and participation links, source and destination groups with the target sharing group, and a dead marker that excludes draining groups.

The cgroup control group is identified by an embedded self state with null subsystem pointer, its filesystem node, hierarchy pointer, depth level and a flexible ancestor chain that includes itself. Capacity state tracks visible and dying descendants against a maximum plus split populated domain and threaded child counts, a threaded total and a kill sequence. Control state holds configured and effective child subsystem masks with prior values, an RCU protected per subsystem vector with per subsystem dying tallies, domain ancestry with a transitional prior value, and links for task sharing groups in both directions. Accounting keeps per processor statistic bases separated by cache padding from global totals and prior processor time. User and lifecycle state provides process, event and pressure file handles, on demand identifier lists, offline waiting, release work, pressure tracking, packet filter storage, freezer state and optional extended storage and scheduler hooks.

The cgroup_freezer_state separates a desired frozen request from an effective frozen decision, with counts of frozen descendants and of tasks considered frozen including stopped and traced tasks, plus a sequence protected start timestamp and accumulated frozen duration. The cgroup_root hierarchy root pairs its filesystem root with an attached subsystem mask, a unique hierarchy identifier, active list linkage and RCU head, a group count for reporting, option flags, a release agent path and name buffers, ending with the embedded root group required to sit last because of the trailing flexible ancestor array.

Hierarchy linkage through sibling and children lists is safe under cgroup_mutex or RCU. Descendant and dying descendant tallies plus the kill sequence allow readers with either cgroup_mutex or css_set_lock but require both for updates. Task accounting, task and iterator lists, group to set links, populated counters and freezer counts with freeze timing are serialized by css_set_lock, while migration endpoints, preload and participation linkage and dying subsystem counts are serialized by cgroup_mutex. Statistic flush scratch state is guarded by rstat_base_lock for self entries and by the subsystem rstat lock otherwise; hot path totals use bsync, freeze times use freeze_seq with css_set_lock for writers, identifier lists use pidlist_mutex, and control file state uses its own spin lock with teardown deferred via work and RCU.

The ancestor chain is a trailing flexible array, so the group structure must remain the last member of its hierarchy root and sizing must account for depth. The per subsystem vector in a sharing group is immutable after creation except for the initial set during boot registration, and effective states may point at ancestors when controllers are disabled, requiring reverse membership handling. A dead sharing group must be skipped during migration. Parents must stay online while children are online via the online counter, child iteration relies on monotonic serial order to allow resume, and destruction must pass through reference release into work based reclamation to avoid use after free.
